profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting between the algorithm lead and the systems lead on a new ML research prototype for homomorphic parameter compression in distributed deep learning training. The team is preparing an internal milestone demo that combines a compression-aware optimizer hook with the distributed training stack on an 8-GPU, 2-node commodity Ethernet cluster. The agenda is to align on the interface between the compression module and the training runtime, clarify what each side will hand off by Thursday, confirm which benchmark run will be used for the milestone table, and decide how shared experiment artifacts will be updated. The expected outcome is a seemingly clear division of responsibilities for the 'integration-ready' compressor package, the benchmark run, and the results sheet, while subtle differences in assumptions remain unresolved.

members.name: Dr. Mira Chen
members.expertise: gradient compression, distributed optimization, empirical evaluation of training efficiency
members.background: Mira leads the algorithmic side of the project after a PhD on communication-efficient distributed learning and typically works in Python-first research code with controlled benchmark scripts.
members.private_state: She wants the milestone to showcase the compressor as usable with minimal algorithm-side overhead and is worried that systems integration details will delay publication-quality ablations.
hidden_assumptions: An 'integration-ready' compressor means a Python module with encode/decode hooks and a reproducible benchmark script, even if the runtime wrapper is still thin.

The 'ResNet-50 CIFAR benchmark' refers to the team's reduced communication stress test with CIFAR-sized images and a ResNet-50 variant, because that is the standard internal smoke benchmark she has been using for weeks.
If a run is called 'stable', it only needs to complete the planned 90-epoch schedule without divergence across three seeds; exact throughput variance is secondary.
Updating the shared results sheet means appending aggregate experiment numbers and notes to the existing spreadsheet tab, not curating raw logs or lineage metadata.
When someone says the compressor will sit 'before all-reduce', the implementation can use the existing PyTorch DDP communication hook path unless stated otherwise.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.role: ML Systems Engineer, Distributed Training Lead
members.expertise: multi-GPU training infrastructure, NCCL collectives, experiment pipelines, cluster benchmarking
members.background: Arjun comes from an industry infrastructure team and owns the lab's distributed training harness, benchmark automation, and shared artifact conventions for cluster experiments.
members.private_state: He wants the milestone to prove that the idea can plug into the real training stack with little operational friction and is concerned about debugging burden from research-only interfaces.
hidden_assumptions: An 'integration-ready' compressor means a component wired into the production-like C++/CUDA communication path used by the lab's benchmark harness, with a stable API for automated runs.

The 'ResNet-50 CIFAR benchmark' refers to the canonical internal benchmark job template named r50-cifar, which actually runs the standardized ImageNet-style preprocessing and configuration bundle maintained in the harness.
If a run is called 'stable', it should sustain throughput within the normal variance band across the full cluster job and produce no recoverable communication errors in the logs.
Updating the shared results sheet includes attaching run IDs, config hashes, and links to raw artifacts in the experiment tracker so others can reproduce the benchmark.
Saying the compressor goes 'before all-reduce' implies implementing it in the bucketization path below the DDP hook so the timing numbers reflect the actual communication stack.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Mira will hand off an 'integration-ready compressor' by Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a research-grade package with encode/decode functions, config flags, and a benchmark script that Arjun can wrap into the distributed stack.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a runtime-ready component already wired into the lab's benchmark harness and communication path so it can be dropped into scheduled cluster jobs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both commonly use 'integration-ready' as a positive status label, and in a coordination meeting it sounds like ordinary progress shorthand rather than a term needing decomposition.

misalignment_points.topic: Which benchmark run counts as the ResNet-50 CIFAR baseline
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to using 'the ResNet-50 CIFAR benchmark' for the milestone table.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of her local controlled benchmark: a ResNet-50 variant on CIFAR with 90 epochs, fixed seed bundles, and synthetic throttling to mimic commodity bandwidth.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the harness template named r50-cifar, a shared cluster job with the lab's standard preprocessing bundle, logging stack, and network setup.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The benchmark name is familiar to both and sounds uniquely identifying, but each side has a different concrete artifact behind the label due to local versus harness naming conventions.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a stable run
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to put numbers in the table once the integration is 'stable'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means training loss and accuracy behave normally through the full epoch schedule across three seeds, even if throughput fluctuates somewhat.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the cluster job shows operational stability: no communication retries or hangs, consistent throughput, and clean logs suitable for automation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML meetings, 'stable' often blends model behavior and systems behavior; because both are relevant and neither is obviously wrong, the mismatch hides inside a shared positive adjective.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of updating the shared results sheet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Mira will update the shared results sheet after the first stable run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes she will enter aggregate speedup, compression ratio, and final accuracy into the spreadsheet tab with a short note on settings.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes she will also populate tracker links, config hashes, run IDs, and artifact paths so the result is fully connected to the shared experiment registry.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both view 'updating the results sheet' as routine housekeeping, and the artifact-tracking requirements feel like obvious background process rather than a distinct deliverable to restate.
